key_insight: 3D Point Splatting (3DPS) is the first radar renderer that is simultaneously physically faithful, complex-valued, and efficient enough for multi-view mmWave novel view synthesis.
engineering_relevance: It lets one optimized radar scene generate ADC, complex range profiles, and range-azimuth outputs from the same model, reducing retraining and improving deployability for radar perception pipelines.
method: Uses oriented 3D points with an ITU-R P.2040 material model evaluated in closed form.
Derives rendering directly from the radar equation and splats complex phasors into range bins via a precomputed point spread function.
Supports standard FFT pipelines to produce ADC, CRP, and RA outputs from the same optimized scene.
evidence_signal: On six outdoor ColoRadar scenes, 3DPS achieved 0.587 mean Pearson correlation on held-out RA images and outperformed three optical-NVS baselines by 1.7x to 5.2x, with ~3 minutes training per scene on an RTX 4090.
watch_item: Performance is reported on a specific outdoor dataset, so generalization to other radar setups, materials, and sensing geometries may require additional validation.
paper_title: 3D Point Splatting for mmWave Radar Novel View Synthesis
